metadata.copyrightInfo: © 2026 Flying Particles, Inc. For Flying Particles club use only. Expanded checklist for instruction based on the 1979 Piper PA-28-161 Warrior II POH VB-1180 (required by STC SA00397NY) and the FPI Piper PA28 Checkout Form rev. 11/18/2026

items.prompt: # reflects an entry on the PA28 checkout form rev. 11/18/2026.
N2933A is a PA-28-161 (160 HP, fixed pitch). STC SA00397NY raises max weight to 2,440 lb. Speeds are KIAS.
Electric fuel pump, fixed pitch, no MP gauge: set power by RPM. GTN 650 with analog CDI.
BATT and ALT switches are reversed: BATT is on the LEFT, ALT on the RIGHT.
TBC: propeller model (sets static RPM) and whether an alternate static source is installed.
Speeds per POH VB-1180. Short field landing speeds are from the landing distance chart (Fig. 5-35).
FLOW: cockpit, then right wing, nose, left wing, tail, then back in the cockpit. Fuel and oil every flight.
Gauges are only a guide: look in the tanks.
Flaps lock and carry weight on the step only when fully up.
Look in the tank. A full tank is 24 gal usable, and 17 gal is the bottom of the filler neck tab.
Club rule: add one quart when it falls to 5 quarts. Seat the dipstick properly.
Lift the stall detector on the left wing leading edge: the horn should sound. The pitot head gets hot.
BATT is the LEFT switch, ALT the RIGHT switch.
Three strokes is the club practice for N2933A. If it does not start in 5 to 10 seconds, prime and try again.
No oil pressure in 30 seconds: shut down. Limit cranking to 30 seconds with a 2 minute rest.
Warm up no more than 2 minutes in warm weather, 4 in cold. Avoid prolonged idling.
Club practice: lean on the ground to avoid plug fouling. Full rich again before takeoff.
Differential 50 RPM maximum. One magneto no longer than 10 seconds.
Avoid prolonged ground operation with carburetor heat on: the air is unfiltered.
Warm enough when the throttle opens without faltering. Pump OFF proves the engine pump.
TBC by propeller: 74DM6-0-60 2330 to 2430 RPM, 74DM6-0-58 2365 to 2465 RPM (sea level, ISA).
Takeoff trim is slightly aft of neutral. Raising the nose early delays liftoff.
Rotate 40 to 52, obstacle 44 to 57 by weight. 52 and 57 are at max weight.
The POH also has a flaps up short field takeoff with the same speeds.
No obstacle: accelerate just above the ground straight to 79 KIAS.
Best economy: throttle full open, set RPM with mixture. Never lean above 75% power for over 15 seconds.
Alternate tanks: one for 1 hour after takeoff, then the other 2 hours. Fuel pump ON to switch, then OFF. Never run a tank dry.
In a long power off descent, clear the engine by opening and closing the throttle.
Full rich at low airports (POH). At high elevation airports set best power instead: full rich loses power for a go around.
Heat reduces power, which matters in a go around. Full throttle with heat on can cause detonation.
Braking is most effective with flaps up and back pressure on the wheel.
The POH has no separate go around checklist: this follows its flap and climb speeds.
Loop the seat belt through the control wheel and pull it snug (POH).
Refuel if over 1 tach hour since last fill.
Ice shows as a drop in RPM. Expect more roughness as it melts, then smoothness.
Complete loss may be oil exhaustion or a bad gauge. The engine may stop suddenly.
BATT is the LEFT switch, ALT the RIGHT switch.
The ALT light may glow with a light load and charged battery. The battery is the only power if the alternator fails.
BATT is the LEFT switch, ALT the RIGHT switch.
Overload means alternator output over 20 amps above known load. ALT ON with BATT OFF only for an electrical failure.
Both open: close the side latch, then the top. A partly open door still flies normally.
Overpriming is the usual cause. If it starts, keep it running to pull the fire in.
After fuel exhaustion, power may take up to 10 seconds to return after switching tanks.
Lose excess altitude by widening the pattern, flaps or slips. Touch down at the lowest safe speed.
Increase airspeed to help extinguish an engine fire.
